title: Cluster 03 DRILL: Species, Speciation and Phylogeny
subtitle: H2 Biology 9477 · Book 7 · 8 questions · 73 marks · 29 parts · one mark per minute, so a little over an hour and a quarter · every question is an actual exam paper question
intro_html:
Answers sit directly under each part, hidden. Click Show answer only after you have said your full reasoning aloud for that part. Check (a) before you start (b), that is the point of the layout.

Rate your confidence before every reveal. A dashed line sits above each answer block. Say high, medium or guessed out loud before you click. A right answer said hesitantly stays ACTIVE; a right answer said confidently moves on.

Every question below is a real exam paper question. The stem is the paper's own wording. Where a stem has been edited it is only so that it stands without the parts of the original that came before it, and the edit is written out in the Sources block at the foot of that question.

Eight questions, 73 marks, 29 parts. This cluster owns five of Core Idea 4's fourteen outcomes, 4(h), 4(i), 4(j), 4(k) and 4(l), and it is where the marks are. The phylogeny and classification heading is the largest in the whole Book, and it is the heading the official specimen leaned on hardest.

Question 6 is the whole of Book 7's presence inside 9477 Specimen Paper 3 Question 1. A multiple sequence alignment for six primates, a ranking, an explanation of your own method, and a histogram of pairwise mtDNA differences. LO 4(l) names multiple sequence alignment outright and the specimen delivered it as this Book's highest-value block. If one thing in Book 7 is drilled to fluency, it is this.

Question 2 is the full-cycle question. Part (a) runs allopatric speciation end to end on a figure you have never seen, with no scaffolding and the command word Suggest; part (c) runs the same model with the barrier supplied by timing rather than geography.

Nine real figures, six questions figure-led. Tree reading and relatedness ranking is an archetype with no analogue anywhere else in the syllabus, so it is drilled here deliberately and at length. Every figure is the real image from the paper it came from, not a redrawing.

Two MCQs, both real, both audited. Both are figure-led and both are relatedness reading, but one is an immunological precipitate scale and the other is a radial tree, so the reasoning is different in each.

What the marks reward. Write viable, fertile offspring in full; both adjectives do work. Reach reproductive isolation, never stop at geographical separation. Count differences, not similarities, and say the count. Never read a tree as a timeline, and never say one tip evolved from the tip next to it. Quote figures off any graph you are told to refer to.

One primary concept each, checked for duplicated required answers as well as duplicated labels. Q1 the species concept and what it cannot do · Q2 speciation end to end, once with a geographical barrier and once with a temporal one · Q3 the barriers themselves, prezygotic and postzygotic · Q4 classification against phylogeny, and the clause that separates them · Q5 five different ways of reading relatedness off a figure · Q6 the specimen's own alignment block · Q7 why molecular methods win and where they stop working · Q8 the three classification methods and their limitations, at essay length. Declared overlaps, and there are three. The advantages of molecular methods are stated in Q4(d) as a one-mark reason, argued in Q7(a) as a two-mark explain, and set against their limitations in Q8 at essay length; the three schemes score different things. Multiple sequence alignment appears in Q6(d) as the method you must explain performing and in Q7(b) as the phrase its scheme makes compulsory. Reproductive isolation appears in Q1 as the definition's test, in Q2 as the endpoint of speciation and in Q3 as the barriers themselves; no two of those schemes accept the same answer.

Nothing from Cluster 1 or Cluster 2, and nothing from Books 8 or 9. Variation, natural selection, the three modes, homology as evidence, the fossil record, drift, gene flow, heterozygote advantage and Hardy-Weinberg are all tested in the first two drills and none of them is required here. Out of scope under 9477 and therefore absent: polyploidy, the four non-biological species concepts, binomial nomenclature and Linnaeus, cladistics vocabulary, adaptive radiation and mass extinction, and the distance-matrix formalism. All of them are not in the learning outcomes.
